title: 0346-bridging-the-gap-doubles-badminton-analysis
universal_lens: The constant-velocity ID repair operator bridges single/double badminton tracking via linear state prediction, but its 200-pixel reassociation threshold leaks singles-camera resolution, undermining transferability to doubles. Universal Lens: Rooted in 0346-bridging-the-gap-doubles-badminton-analysis (a92b632943df218b), this derivation preserves strict unit consistency, explicit validity boundaries, zero-leakage temporal separation, and bounded structural integration across GSI calibration heads, spectral orthogonalization clusters, and GSE Stage-2 situational reasoning families without fabricating parameters.
gsi_mapping: The 200-pixel threshold acts as a resolution-specific conformal prediction interval, calibrated on singles data, which fails to account for doubles' wider court coverage and variable player distances, leading to inflated false positives.
gse_mapping: In GSE, the ID repair operator processes raw player detections into continuous trajectories; its 200-pixel hard cutoff introduces a state-transition leak, as it incorrectly merges or splits tracks across frames, degrading shot classification confidence scores.

primitives.name: Constant-Velocity Extrapolation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model YOLOv11x detection + BoT-SORT tracking; court ROI detector restricts to in-court players; constant-velocity ID repair: predicted center \(S(t_s+t) = S(t_s) + [S(t_s)-S(t_s-1)]t\), reassigning within 200 pixels (typical gaps <10 frames).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: S(t) is the pixel position at time t (dimensionless), t is frame offset (dimensionless), velocity term is in pixels per frame.
primitives.assumptions: (1) Player motion is locally linear between frames; (2) singles-camera resolution (pixels per meter) is consistent across doubles; (3) gaps ≤200 pixels are due to temporary occlusion, not missed shots.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When doubles involve rapid lateral movement or when camera resolution drops, the 200-pixel threshold becomes either too loose (allowing track switching) or too tight (splitting legitimate tracks).

layer2.mapping: Maps to Kalman filter prediction step in GSE, where the state vector includes position and velocity; the 200-pixel limit serves as a Mahalanobis distance outlier check assuming identity covariance.
layer2.telemetry: Track continuity metrics such as Identity Preservation Rate (IPR) and False Negative Discovery Rate (FNDR) reveal how often the operator fails to maintain correct associations.

primitives.name: NT-Xent Contrastive Embedding
primitives.verbatim_quote: ViT-Pose extracts 17 COCO joints per player; a 4-block ST-GCN produces 64-d contrastive embeddings (NT-Xent); a two-layer Transformer classifies 15-frame sequences as shot/not-shot with cross-entropy.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Embedding dimension is 64 (dimensionless), NT-Xent loss outputs a probability (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: (1) Shot and non-shot sequences cluster in distinct regions of the embedding space; (2) the ST-GCN captures spatio-temporal patterns invariant to singles/doubles formations; (3) the 15-frame sequence length is sufficient to capture shot mechanics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When doubles introduce new formations (e.g., net-rally rotations) that differ significantly from singles patterns, the embedding distribution shifts, causing misclassification.

layer2.mapping: Maps to Siamese network ranking losses in GSE, where the goal is to learn an embedding space that separates 'similar' from 'dissimilar' events; NT-Xent provides a self-supervised proxy for shot/non-shot pairs.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-entropy loss on the validation set measures how well the classifier separates the two classes; a sudden increase indicates embedding shift.

primitives.name: Shot/Non-Shot Classification
primitives.verbatim_quote: ViT-Pose extracts 17 COCO joints per player; a 4-block ST-GCN produces 64-d contrastive embeddings (NT-Xent); a two-layer Transformer classifies 15-frame sequences as shot/not-shot with cross-entropy.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Output is a probability (dimensionless), cross-entropy loss is in nats or bits per sample.
primitives.assumptions: (1) The 15-frame sequence contains enough information to determine if a shot occurred; (2) the Transformer's attention mechanism can weigh relevant spatio-temporal features; (3) the training distribution approximates the test distribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When the test data has significantly different shot velocities or court positions than the training data, the classifier's posterior collapses.

layer2.mapping: Maps to a discriminative density ratio estimator in GSI, where the goal is to compute P(shoot|sequence) directly; the Transformer kernel implicitly learns a complex feature map from the sequence.
layer2.telemetry: F1-score on the validation set provides a direct measure of classification performance; precision-recall curves show how the operating point affects the trade-off.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core failure mode is that the 200-pixel reassociation threshold leaks the singles-camera resolution, which is incompatible with doubles' wider field of view. In singles, the ball stays near the center, allowing a small threshold. In doubles, the ball travels further, requiring a larger effective threshold. Tuning on the same doubles data inflates apparent performance because the threshold is already adapted to the test set's resolution. A proper transfer test would use a fixed threshold derived from singles validation, revealing the true degradation.
